faq.q: How can the same power be carried at high voltage?
faq.a: Electrical power is voltage times current. So a million watts could be 1000 volts at 1000 amps, or 100,000 volts at just 10 amps. Raising the voltage lets the current fall.
asks: What is electrical power equal to?

faq.q: Why does a big current waste energy in cables?
faq.a: Current heats any wire, and the heat goes up with the square of the current. Ten times less current means a hundred times less heat wasted along the line.

faq.q: How is the voltage lowered before it reaches homes?
faq.a: Substations and smaller transformers step the voltage down in stages, finally to about 230 volts in the UK and Europe, or 120 volts in North America.

faq.q: How high is the voltage on big power lines?
faq.a: Main transmission lines in the UK run at 275,000 or 400,000 volts, and some countries use over 700,000 volts. That is why pylons are so tall and their insulators so long.
asks: How many volts are in a pylon line?

faq.q: Why are power lines dangerous to go near?
faq.a: At such high voltage, electricity can jump through the air to a kite string, a ladder or a person who gets too close. Always stay well away and never fly kites near power lines.
asks: Can electricity jump from power lines?

facts: UK main transmission lines run at 275,000 or 400,000 volts.

quiz.say: If the current in a power line is cut to a tenth, what happens to the heat lost?
quiz.show: If the current in a power line is cut to a tenth, what happens to the heat lost?
quiz.why: Heat loss depends on the current squared, so a tenth of the current gives a tenth times a tenth, a hundredth of the heat.

wrong.1: That forgets the loss depends on the square of the current.
wrong.2: Less current always means less heating in the wire.
